sents.t: In January, Lily’s bakery took over our lives.
Every evening after work, I went over to Oak Street to help her fix up the old flower shop.
First, we cleared out the boxes that the last owner had left behind.
Then Carlos and Danny came over to put up shelves, and Ana and Emma helped us paint the walls a soft yellow.
The biggest problem was the oven.
It broke down twice in one week.
“Maybe this was a bad idea,” she said, sitting on the floor covered in flour.
“You can’t give up now,” I told her.
“You’ve been dreaming about this for years.”
Gus, who can fix anything, came over and found the problem in ten minutes.
We also had to fill out a lot of forms for the city.
An inspector came to check out the kitchen.
He looked around for an hour, wrote some notes, and finally said, “Everything looks good.”
Lily came up with the name: Sunrise Bakery.
“Because bakers get up before the sun,” she laughed.
Late on Friday night, we turned off the lights and looked around at the shelves, the tables, and the big new sign.
